newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sammi to take steps to reduce debt - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Sammi to take steps to reduce debt - chairman.

text.p: Sammi Group Chairman Kim Hyun-bae, promising steps to sell real estate and other Sammi assets to reduce debt, said he was confident the conglomerate's corporate structure would improve in the near future.
"I am confident we will achieve business normalisation in a fairly short period of time," Kim told a news conference.
Five units of Sammi Group, one of South Korea's 30 largest industrial conglomerates, have filed for court receivership to protect them from their debts.
Sammi group has a total debt of 1.65 trillion won, a Sammi spokesman said.
The five include flagship Sammi Steel Co and its trading arm Sammi Corp.

Asked why Sammi firms sought court protection, the chairman said it was not easy to sell off real estate quickly. He said his group could no longer handle rising banking costs while it faced difficulty in securing fresh loans.
"I believe it was the only was to minimise negative effects," Kim said referring to court receivership.
He said he would give up all his shares in Sammi firms and take steps to help strengthen Sammi's financial status. Details of his shareholding were not immediately available.
